title: Normalized derived Cech descent followed by exact inverse image
statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\mathcal B$ be topoi of sheaves on small sites in fixed larger coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Give them sheaves of commutative rings and module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $h:\mathcal B\to\mathcal Y$ be morphisms of ringed topoi with Cartesian coefficient identifications, so that their module inverse images are exact. Let $v:V\to1_{\mathcal X}$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets. Let $\mathcal X_n=\mathcal X/(V^{\times(n+1)})$, with localized coefficient rings, and $v_n:\mathcal X_n\to\mathcal X$ the localization morphisms [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For a module sheaf $K$ on $\mathcal X$ put $K_n=v_n^*K$. Use ordinary total right derived direct images and unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The augmented Cech nerve induces a natural isomorphism
$$h^*Rf_*(K[0])\ \cong\operatorname{Tot}_{n\geq0}\bigl(h^*R(fv_n)_*(K_n[0])\bigr).$$
The totalization is that of a nonnegative cosimplicial derived object, computed from a compatible first-quadrant resolution with total differential $d_{\mathrm{Cech}}+(-1)^n d_{\mathrm{res}}$ in Cech degree $n$. All diagrams are small. The arrow from the left is the augmentation, degree zero is restriction of sections, and evaluation on $V$ is the direct-image counit. The isomorphism is natural in $K$, in refinements of the covering, and in exact coefficient-restriction functors which commute with the displayed underived direct images and inverse images. Exact inverse image commutes with this first-quadrant totalization: only finitely many terms contribute in each total degree. No assertion that exact inverse image preserves an arbitrary unbounded product totalization is made. Here the cosimplicial derived object includes its coherent resolution model, not just an unspecified diagram in the triangulated homotopy category. For coefficient restriction, naturality is with respect to the canonical right-derived comparison maps; these maps are not asserted to be isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use the constructed coherent model CechColumnAux.model from [lem-sfb-cech-injective-column-model], with its adjunction-defined restrictions and units. Sectionwise evaluation proves additivity of elementModulePullback. The zero extension of each ordinary injective resolution is K-injective by the bounded-below injective criterion. For the column comparison, the exact extension-by-zero adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] implies that element-site restriction preserves injectives; commute restriction with extension and apply the same K-injective criterion. The ordinary right-derived unit is therefore invertible, and its image under H remains invertible.

Apply [lem-sfb-cech-injective-image-augmentation] to the supplied resolution and model. Its total_augmentation field gives b0 with the precise localization-unit components and QuasiIso b0. This is the rowwise injective Cech argument and the first-quadrant augmentation criterion, including degree-zero descent.

In degree r the pairs (n,q) with n+q=r form a finite set, contained in the finite interval below (r,r). Additive H preserves the resulting finite coproducts. The identity on each bicomplex component identifies the bicomplex for F followed by H with H applied to the bicomplex for F. Apply HomologicalComplex2.mapTotalIso to this identification. Its coprojection equation gives exactly the displayed finite_total_comparison, including both differential signs. Define b=H(b0) followed by the inverse total comparison; its components are exactly the localization unit into (0,q).

Exact H preserves the quasi-isomorphism b0, so b and its zero extension are quasi-isomorphisms. The resolutionComparison is invertible: it is H applied to the derived resolution map and the K-injective computing isomorphism, followed by the exact-functor factorization isomorphism. Compose it with Q of mapExtendIso followed by extendMap b, and take the associated isomorphism. Its hom is the required composite by construction, giving derived_cech_image_totalization with unchanged normalization.

For a resolution map, check the augmentation square degreewise using ιTotal_map and naturality of the localization unit. Apply refinement_laws from [lem-sfb-cech-augmentation-normalized-naturality] for the refinement square. For an arbitrary chain homotopy use its signed_total_homotopy, extend by zero, and apply Q_map_eq_of_homotopy. These arguments work for arbitrary supplied complexes and maps, with no extra lifting assumptions.

For coefficient naturality, apply ιTotal_map to the actual coefficientTotalMap. On the (0,q) component the claimed equality is hδ at I.X q followed by naturality of the target localization unit at t.f q. For the derived normalization apply rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_rightDerivedPullback_app, then rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_naturality at t and functoriality of Q. This directly proves the canonical unit equation for the stated general additive functors; no scalar-specific coefficient comparison theorem is required and invertibility is not asserted.
